entries.title: Notifications on your phone and computer
entries.summary: Mentions, sign-off requests, shares and access requests can now ring your phone, tablet or computer, even when Markdrop is closed. Choose one to open the page at that block.
entries.body:
- Turn them on in **Settings › Account › Notifications on your devices**: **Turn on**, allow them when asked, and **Send a test**. Do it on each device you want notified.
- Works in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari on computers and Android. On iPhone and iPad (iOS 16.4 or later) it works in the [installed app](/get-started/install-app).
- Choose a notification to open the page at the block that mentions you. An open Markdrop window goes there; otherwise a new one opens. It's marked read under the bell too.
- **Notify me when** turns mentions, sign-off requests, shares and access requests on or off for all your devices; **Devices** lists every device that gets them, with **Remove**. Signing out stops them on that browser.
- A notification says only what the bell says, only about pages you can still open (checked when it's sent), is encrypted for your device on the way, and several on one page arrive as one.
- See [Push notifications](/pages/mentions-and-notifications#push-notifications).

entries.title: Ask Markdrop everywhere: one assistant, ⌘J, and answers you can insert
entries.summary: One assistant replaces Ask in page, Ask this meeting and Ask across meetings: ✦ Ask in every top bar or ⌘J from anywhere opens Ask Markdrop beside what you're reading, on the right scope (This doc, Meetings, This folder, Workspace or Everything), with one conversation that follows you and Insert to put an answer into the doc.
entries.body:
- **One assistant, everywhere.** ✦ Ask in the top bar of documents, pages, workspaces and folders, ⌘J (Ctrl J) from anywhere, the box on your home, Ask this meeting and the Meetings page all open the same Ask Markdrop: a panel beside what you're reading, a sheet on phones.
- **Scope chips at the top**: This doc, Meetings, This folder, Workspace, Everything. It starts on the one that fits where you are; switch any time. Meetings adds This meeting, a series and a period in the question box.
- **This doc** answers from the doc first, then what your meetings decided about it, then the workspace, and knows the section you're in and what you selected. It works in pages and classic Markdown documents.
- **Insert** puts an answer into the doc, with its sources as links: blocks after your cursor in a page, a paragraph at your cursor in a document you're editing, or the editor opened with it after the section you were reading. Only when you choose it; editors only.
- **One conversation**: ask on your home, open a page, press ⌘J and keep going. Conversations are kept 90 days and listed under the home's box.
- **Ask about this** in From meetings asks about one decision, action item or question.
- Same rules: only what you can open, every source checked again; restricted meetings never reach anyone else. This doc, This folder, Workspace and Everything count towards AI search, Meetings towards Meetings AI, as before.
- **API and MCP**: `POST /api/v1/ask` takes `scope` and `context`; `GET /api/v1/ask/context` lists the scopes offered where you are; `ask_documents` takes `page` and `folder`.

entries.title: Asking meetings is a real conversation; the Meetings page shows what each meeting was about
entries.summary: Ask this meeting and Ask across meetings are now one chat: answers stream in with numbered sources that show who said it, when, and the line itself, with follow-up questions and a conversation that's still there when you come back. The Meetings page lists each meeting with its cover, summary, people and counts.
entries.body:
- **One chat for asking meetings.** Your question on the right, the answer on the left as it's written, with what it's reading while it works. **Stop** (or Esc) ends an answer early.
- **Numbered sources.** Select **1**, **2**… in an answer, or **N sources** under it: each source shows the meeting, its date and series, who spoke and when, and the line itself. **Jump to the moment** opens the transcript there.
- **Follow-ups.** Suggested follow-up questions under each answer, and follow-ups across meetings now know what you asked before.
- **Conversations are kept.** Reopen a meeting, or the Meetings page, and your conversation is still there (on any device you sign in on). **New chat** starts over. If you can no longer open a meeting an answer used, that answer is hidden.
- **Ask across meetings opens beside your meetings** on a computer (or page-wide with **Expand**) and full screen on a phone. Pick a series and a period with the chips in the question box.
- **Keyboard.** Enter sends, Shift+Enter is a new line, ↑ brings back your last question, Esc stops an answer or closes the sources.
- **The Meetings page** shows each meeting's series cover with its date, the day, time and length, a line of the summary, who was there, and how many decisions, action items and open questions it has. Month headings stay on screen as you scroll; search covers titles, series and people; point at a meeting to open its transcript or ask it. Connect Google Meet, Import past meetings, the Meetings folder and Organize are under one calm header.
- **A meeting bar on every meeting page**: who was there, who can open it, **Transcript** and **Ask this meeting**.
- MCP `list_meetings` gives each meeting's summary line and its decision and open-question counts. API: `GET /api/v1/meetings` rows add `summary`, `decisions`, `open_questions` and `cover`; ask citations add `speaker`, `at` and `quote`; both asks take `thread_id` (and Ask across takes `history`) and return `thread_id`, readable with `GET /api/v1/ask/threads/{id}`.

entries.title: Meeting memory while writing: what the team decided, right in the page
entries.summary: While you write a PRD or any page in a workspace, From meetings shows the decisions, action items and open questions your meetings recorded about it, with the date, the meeting and a link to the moment. Insert one as a cited line, get a gentle card when a section leaves out a decision, and ask the page with your meetings.
entries.body:
- **From meetings**, beside **Ask** at the bottom right of a page, follows the section you're writing: decisions, action items (owner, due, open or done), open questions and topics from the workspace's meetings, each with its date, meeting and series, and a link to the moment in the transcript. A search box finds anything else.
- **Insert** adds a dated, cited line, such as "**Decided on Oct 28, 2026** (Daily Standup): …", with a mention of the meeting and a link to the moment. `/meetings` in the page opens the panel and inserts where you typed.
- **Missed decisions.** When a section clearly leaves out a decision about its topic, a small card asks "Include it here?". With AI on, Claude Haiku 5.5 also notices a section that says something different from a decision. Nothing changes unless you choose **Include**. Both the button and the cards can be switched off, per person.
- **Ask the page with your meetings.** **Ask** in a workspace page answers from the page and the workspace's meetings, naming the meeting and date for "when did we decide…" questions, with citations that open the moment.
- **Private by design.** Only meetings you can open count. Meetings restricted to their attendees, including one-to-one calls, never appear for anyone else. No extra AI cost: the memory comes from the summary each meeting already has.
- **For AI apps**: `meeting_context` returns the decisions and action items related to a topic or a page, with dates, links and a cited line to paste (80 MCP tools now).

entries.title: Leaving a page frees it for others at once
entries.summary: When you stop editing a page by leaving it, others can edit it straight away instead of up to 2 minutes later: going to another page, adding a sub-page, closing the tab, and on a workspace's own domain too.
entries.body:
- **Leave and it's free.** Going to another page, opening the sub-page you just added or closing the tab lets go of the page at once. Before, the page could stay marked as yours for up to 2 minutes, and your teammates and their AI apps had to wait.
- **Nothing typed is lost on the way out.** What you typed in the last moment before leaving is saved first, then the page is free.
- **Even when the browser can't say goodbye.** If your browser quits without a word (a crash, a laptop that shut down), the page is free about 10 seconds later.
- **AI apps can write right after you leave.** `update_page` and the other writing tools no longer meet "is editing" from a tab that's already gone.

entries.title: An open page you've left alone no longer blocks anyone
entries.summary: A page counts as being edited only while someone is actually editing it: from their first change until 2 minutes without one, or 60 seconds with their tab in the background. The page's owner and workspace admins can take over with Edit anyway, and nothing the other person typed is lost.
entries.body:
- **Opening a page takes nothing.** Clicking into a page, scrolling or selecting text no longer marks you as editing. Only a real change does, so a tab left open on a page never blocks your teammates or their AI apps.
- **Idle and away release it.** 2 minutes without a change, or 60 seconds with the tab in the background, and the page is free for others. What you typed is saved first, and your next change makes it yours again. The pencil in who's viewing goes at the same moment.
- **Edit anyway.** The page's owner and workspace admins can take a page from whoever is editing it. The other person's editor says who took over, and anything they hadn't saved is kept as a version in the page's history.
- **Clearer refusals.** "Venkat is editing this page (idle for 1 min, unsaved changes). It releases in about 1 min." The same facts come as fields over the API (`idle_s`, `dirty`, `releases_in_s`, `can_take_over`) and MCP.
- **AI apps can take over too.** `update_page`, `replace_section`, `insert_embed`, `set_page_properties`, `set_slug`, `restore_page_version`, `summarize_page` and `update_document` take `take_over: true` for the page's owner or a workspace admin. `get_page` says how idle the person editing is.

entries.title: Meetings import themselves: Connect Google Meet
entries.summary: Connect Google Meet once and every call that Google transcribes or takes notes for becomes a meeting page by itself, about 15 minutes after it ends. A small script in your own Google account does it, read-only, with a token that only imports meetings into one workspace. Manual import stays, side by side.
entries.body:
- **Connect Google Meet** on the Meetings page, next to **Import meeting**: Markdrop writes a Google Apps Script with its own token filled in. Paste it at script.google.com, run `setup` once, and it checks your Drive every 15 minutes.
- **Reads only meeting Docs**: Meet transcripts and Gemini's notes in your Drive, created in the last 48 hours. Read-only: it never edits, moves or deletes anything. Its token works for this one inbox and nothing else, and isn't listed with your API tokens.
- **One meeting per call**: the notes and the transcript, arriving minutes apart, become one page; a Doc you already imported by hand isn't imported again.
- **Connected** shows when it last imported and how many meetings it brought in; **Disconnect** stops it at once. Meetings it imported are marked **Auto**.
- **Past meetings too**: choose the last 7, 30 or 90 days when you connect. They come in oldest first, dated by the call, and quietly: nobody is notified about a meeting that's long over. Run `backfill` in the script to go further back.
- **Restrict to attendees** for every automatic import, chosen when you connect.
- **For AI apps:** `meetings_connection` says whether automatic import is on, and `list_meetings` filters by `source` (`manual`, `auto`, `mcp`) and `since`. `import_meeting` doesn't duplicate a call that's already there (76 MCP tools now).
- **Docs:** Meetings is its own section now: import manually, import automatically, ask, and privacy and cost.

entries.title: Markdrop for Slack: meeting notes, /markdrop, link previews and direct messages
entries.summary: Connect a Slack workspace from Workspace settings › Integrations. Meeting notes go to a channel with Done buttons that tick the action items on the page, /markdrop search and ask answer you privately from what you can open, links preview when the whole channel may see them, and mentions, sign-offs, shares and access requests arrive as direct messages.
entries.body:
- **Meeting notes in a channel:** the summary, decisions and action items of each imported meeting, with a **Done** button per action item that ticks it on the Markdrop page as the person who clicked. Meetings restricted to their attendees are never posted; **Post to Slack** in the meeting panel posts one again.
- **`/markdrop search`, `/markdrop ask` and `/markdrop meetings`:** replies only you see, built only from what your Markdrop account can open.
- **Link previews** for markdrop.in links: a preview when anyone with the link, or everyone in your workspace, may open it (and the channel isn't shared with another organization); otherwise "Markdrop link — sign in to view".
- **Direct messages** for mentions, sign-off requests (choose an option in Slack), shares, and access requests (Approve or Decline in Slack), each one switchable.
- **Link your Slack account** once with Sign in with Slack. Markdrop keeps no Slack token for you; the workspace's app token is encrypted.

entries.title: Meetings: every call becomes a page you can ask
entries.summary: Import a Google Meet transcript, Gemini's meeting notes, or both. Markdrop writes the summary, decisions and action items (and @mentions their owners), keeps the transcript, and answers questions about one meeting or all of them, citing the moment it was said.
entries.body:
- **Import** by pasting, uploading (`.txt`, `.vtt`, `.srt`, `.sbv`, `.docx`), or picking Google Meet's transcript and Gemini notes from your Drive. Notes and a transcript of the same call become one meeting.
- **A page per meeting** in the workspace's new **Meetings** folder, with Date, Type, Attendees, Organizer, Duration and Action items as properties: a summary, decisions, an action-item checklist that @mentions and notifies the members who own them, open questions, topics, and the transcript as a sub-page with a line per turn.
- **Google's notes, as written.** When Gemini's notes are there, their summary, details and next steps are used word for word; AI only fills the gaps.
- **Ask this meeting** and **Ask across meetings**: answers in English, with chips that open the transcript at the moment it was said. Only meetings you can open are ever used.
- **Restrict to attendees**, and delete (the importer, or a workspace admin for any meeting).
- **Meetings AI** has its own budget ($5 a day, $50 a month), in the admin's AI tab.
- **For AI apps:** `import_meeting`, `list_meetings`, `get_meeting` and `ask_meetings` (75 MCP tools now).

entries.title: Analytics tells you what changed, answers questions, and shows what people couldn't find
entries.summary: The analytics home has ✦ Insights: what changed in the period and the likely reason, a box to ask your analytics in plain words, and Write this next, which groups what people searched for and didn't find into pages worth writing.
entries.body:
- **Insights** sums up the period in 3 to 5 sentences: what changed and the likely cause (a link, a site that sent people, a new version, devices or countries), each linking to where to look. Written once a day; **Refresh** writes it again. See [Insights and Ask](/analytics/overview#insights-and-ask).
- **Ask your analytics**: type a question like "Which link did best this month?". The AI picks from a fixed set of queries Markdrop runs on your own links and answers with links.
- **Write this next** (workspace owners and admins, and people with their own Guides): searches that found nothing or that nobody opened, and guide questions Ask AI couldn't answer, grouped into topics with an outline. **Create page from this outline** starts the page. See [What people couldn't find](/analytics/content-gaps).
- Workspace searches are now kept without who searched, for 90 days, to power this. See [Privacy at Markdrop](/security/privacy#what-searching-a-workspace-records).
- The weekly analytics email gets the same summary, once it starts sending.
- New MCP tools: `analytics_story`, `ask_analytics` and `content_gaps`. All use Claude Haiku 5.5 and count towards your AI limits; only totals and your own titles are sent, never who visited.

entries.title: ✦ Insights: AI says why people stop, and what to change
entries.summary: A link's Content, Pages, Video and Versions tabs get ✦ Insights: Claude Haiku 5.5 reads the numbers (and your own content) and comes back with three to five findings that point at the exact section, moment, page or version, with rewrites, chapters and a version verdict.
entries.body:
- **Why did they stop?** On a document or page's **Content** tab: where readers leave and why, from section reach, time and the text of those sections, with a **suggested rewrite** to copy, or, on a page you can edit, **Apply in page**: it's offered over that section and nothing changes until you accept.
- **Video and audio coach.** Up to six key moments where people drop, skip or rewatch, with a small frame of each, become timestamped suggestions: cuts, reorders, pacing and **suggested chapters** to copy. Choose a time to mark it on the **Who's still watching** chart.
- **PDF coach.** The pages where readers stop or linger, with their text, and what to cut, move or summarise.
- **Version verdict.** On **Versions**: which version works better, with a **High**, **Medium** or **Low** confidence that Markdrop computes from the sessions, not the AI.
- Needs at least 20 sessions; analyses are saved per period, shared with your AI assistant, and marked out of date when you change the document (**Re-analyse**).
- Only the numbers and your own content are sent, never anything about your readers; encrypted links never send content. Counts towards your AI limits; admins see it as **Analytics AI** with its own caps.
- MCP: the new `analyze_document_engagement` tool (71 tools now, with this release's `analytics_story`, `ask_analytics` and `content_gaps`). API: `GET` / `POST /api/v1/me/documents/{slug}/analytics/ai/{kind}`. See [AI insights for one link](/analytics/ai-insights).

entries.title: CLI 0.6.1: markdrop search looks inside your content
entries.summary: markdrop search now uses the same global search as the app: it finds words inside pages, documents and file contents, forgives typos, and shows the text that matched.
entries.body:
- **`markdrop search`** runs on the app's global search: titles, headings, body text and file contents (HTML and PDF text), folders, workspaces and Guides pages, forgiving typos.
- A new **`guide`** kind for `--kind`, and a **MATCHED** column with the text that matched. `--limit` is now the total number of results (20 by default, at most 50).
- Against a server without the new search it falls back to the titles-only search of 0.6.0.
- Update with `brew upgrade markdrop`, or see [Install the markdrop CLI](/cli/install).

entries.title: Cards show what's inside
entries.summary: The workspace Cards view now previews every item: a page's cover and first blocks, the start of a document, a PDF's first page, images, video posters, a sheet's first cells, and HTML files live when you point at them.
entries.body:
- **Pages** show their cover, icon, title and first blocks. **Markdown documents** show their start, with headings, lists, to-dos, quotes and code.
- **HTML files** show their opening text. Point at the card for a moment and the real page plays, scaled down, in a sandbox on Markdrop's separate files address. A few play at once, with a mouse only.
- **PDFs** show their first page, **images** themselves, **videos** their poster frame and length, **spreadsheets and CSVs** their first cells, **text files** their first lines and **Word documents** their first paragraphs.
- **Fast and quiet.** Previews load only for the cards on screen, after the folder opens, so folders still open straight away. List and Grid are unchanged.
- **Access first.** A card previews only what you could open yourself. End-to-end encrypted documents show a lock, and other items' titles never appear in a preview.
- **AI apps.** `list_workspace_items` takes `previews: true` and adds each item's opening text.
- **API.** `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{id}/items/previews` returns the previews for up to 12 items.
- **Cards is now the default view** for anyone who hasn't picked one; List and Grid are one click away, and your choice is remembered on each device.

entries.title: Files: one top bar, like documents and pages
entries.summary: Leave full screen on a file (an HTML page, a PDF, a sheet, a video, an image) and you get a single bar at the top: the app's header and the file's bar under it are now one, and the file gets the room.
entries.body:
- **One bar.** On the left: the logo (your workspace's logo on its own domain) and the file's title with its type, after the workspace and folder if you're a member. On the right: who's viewing, **Download**, **Read full screen**, **Share** (or **Copy link**), **More artifact actions** (**⋯**), **Create** and your avatar, or **Sign in**.
- **Nothing moved out of reach.** **⋯** starts with the file's size, views and date, then **Copy link** (when **Share** is in the bar), **Settings** (the title, link, password, expiry, the file and its versions), **Replace file**, **Report**, **Delete artifact** and **Remove me**, as before.
- **On your workspace's domain** the owner shares with people right there, and **⋯** has **General access on markdrop.in**, **Settings on markdrop.in** and **Delete on markdrop.in**.
- **On a phone** the bar keeps the title, full screen and **⋯** (with **Share** first), and **Copy link** and **Download** stay in the bar at the bottom.
- The file still opens in its own sandboxed frame on a separate domain; nothing about how it's served changed.

entries.title: Working together on a page: merged changes, no silent overwrites
entries.summary: When two people, or a person and an AI app, change the same page, changes to different parts are merged instead of asking you to throw one away. Open pages catch up after sleep or a dropped connection, follow a rename, and say when a page was deleted or your access changed.
entries.body:
- **Merged, not overwritten.** A save that meets a newer version merges your change into it: different paragraphs, list items or properties both stay. Only when you both changed the same lines does a banner ask, with **Keep both**, **Use theirs** or **Use mine**; their other changes stay either way.
- **Unsaved changes from earlier.** **Restore them** merges your old unsaved changes into the page as it is now, instead of saving the old copy over newer edits.
- **Catching up.** After your laptop sleeps, your connection drops or Markdrop restarts, an open page checks for changes made meanwhile, shows them, and saves what you typed offline.
- **Renamed, deleted, access changed.** A page renamed while you have it open saves what you typed and moves to its new address (it used to stay on **Saving…**). A deleted page says so. Removed from a workspace, or made a viewer, your open pages check again at once.
- **Sub-pages and views.** New, moved and deleted sub-pages show up under **Pages inside** on everyone's open copy. Two people changing a folder's saved views at once both keep their changes.
- **AI apps.** `update_document` takes `base_rev` (the `rev` that `get_document` now returns), so an app can't overwrite a change made after it read the document. Every write tool takes an optional `idempotency_key`: a retry with the same key returns the first result instead of writing twice.

See [Working together on a page](/pages/working-together).

entries.title: AI apps can rename, move and delete folders, and folders never get a silent -2
entries.summary: Three new MCP tools: rename_folder, move_folder and delete_folder, for workspace admins, as in the app. A new folder whose address is already taken is refused, with what holds it, instead of quietly becoming name-2. A renamed or moved folder's old address now redirects.
entries.body:
- **`delete_folder`** deletes an empty folder (to Trash for 30 days). A folder with anything in it is refused, and the error lists what's inside: subfolders, the items you can open, and a count of the rest. Choose `contents: "move_to_parent"` to move everything up one level first, or `contents: "trash"` to send the folder with everything in it to Trash. `restore_document` with the folder's id brings it back.
- **`rename_folder`** and **`move_folder`**: the folder's old address and the old addresses of everything in it redirect to the new ones on your domain.
- **No silent -2.** `create_folder`, and **New folder**, **Rename folder…** and **Move folder to…** in the app, refuse an address that a folder, page, document or file already has in that place, and say what holds it. An item you can't open is never named and never blocks you: the folder takes the next free address, and MCP's result says so. For a suffixed address, pass `on_conflict: "suffix"` (MCP and API).
- **Old folder addresses redirect.** Renaming or moving a folder used to leave its own page's old address empty. It now redirects to where the folder is, and so do the addresses of its subfolders.
- `list_folders` gives each folder's id, address and parent, which the folder tools take (79 MCP tools now).

entries.title: Ask Markdrop: one question across everything you can open
entries.summary: A box at the top of your home asks across your meetings, documents, pages, files and Guides at once. Answers cite their sources (meeting moments included), follow-ups stay in a conversation, and suggested questions catch you up on the week or list your open action items.
entries.body:
- **One box, everything you can open**: meetings and their transcripts, documents, pages, files and Guides. Every source is a number you can tap; meeting chips open the transcript at the moment it was said.
- **Follow-ups** in the same conversation ("and the annual discount?"). **New question** starts over; the conversation is in the address, so reload and Back keep your place.
- **Suggested questions**: **Catch me up on this week**, **My open action items** (every unchecked task that @mentions you, meeting action items included; no AI needed when there are none) and one about your latest meeting.
- **Recent questions** under the box, private to you, kept 90 days.
- **Strict access**: only items you can open now are read; every cited source is checked again before you see it and when you reopen a conversation, and an answer whose sources you lost is hidden. Restricted meetings, encrypted items and workspaces with AI off are never read.
- Built for phones: the first thing on the home, a 16px field and 44px targets.
- Uses the **AI search** budget. MCP `ask_documents` now asks the same way, with `thread_id` for follow-ups and `intent` (`catch_up`, `my_actions`). API: `POST /api/v1/ask` and `/api/v1/ask/threads`.

entries.title: Connect Google Meet finds the meetings someone else organized, and shows what it found
entries.summary: The Google Meet script now imports every meeting you attended: Docs shared with you (a call your manager organized lives in their Drive), shared drives and Google's titles in other languages. Each run reports what it found and why it skipped Docs, right on the Meetings page.
entries.body:
- **Meetings shared with you, on by default**: Google saves a call's transcript and Gemini notes in the organizer's Drive and shares them with attendees. The first script only looked at Docs you own, so an attendee got nothing. **Include meetings shared with me** in the Connect dialog (on by default). A call several attendees send is imported once.
- **More of Google's titles**: "Notes by Gemini" anywhere in the title, Google's names in other languages ("Transcripción", "Notizen von Gemini"…), Docs in a **Meet Recordings** folder, and shared drives.
- **See what the script found**: under **Google Meet connected**, "Script ran 5 min ago · found 2 meeting Docs · 14 skipped: 12 not titled like Meet…", and any Doc it couldn't read. Only counts reach Markdrop, never the skipped Docs.
- **`check`** in Apps Script lists what the script would send and why it skips the rest, without sending anything.
- **Update your script**: scripts installed before today show **New script**. Select **Get the new script**, paste it over `Code.gs` in the same project and run `setup` (the manifest is unchanged).
- API: `POST /api/v1/meetings/inbox/status` (the script's runs), `include_shared` on `POST /api/v1/meetings/connection`, and the script's last run, `needs_update` and `latest_script_version` on `GET /api/v1/meetings/connection`.

entries.title: Markdrop on phones and tablets
entries.summary: Markdrop works like a mobile app: install it on your phone, tablet or computer, and every screen (My files, workspaces, pages, files, the Guides studio, published guides and Analytics) fits a finger, from a small Android phone to an iPad Pro.
entries.body:
- **Install the app**: **Install app** in the account menu puts Markdrop on your home screen or dock, opens on your dashboard, and shows a branded screen when you're offline. See [Install Markdrop as an app](/changelog/install-markdrop-app).
- **My files, workspaces, folders, settings, sharing and search**: nothing scrolls sideways, a tap anywhere on a row or card opens it, and menus open as sheets on phones. See [The app on phones and tablets](/changelog/phones-and-tablets-app).
- **Pages, documents and files**: covers keep their proportions, the New page gallery fits every screen, tablets get the editing toolbar above the keyboard, and PDFs zoom with two fingers. See [Pages, documents and files fit phones and tablets](/changelog/pages-on-phones-and-tablets).
- **Markdrop Guides and Analytics**: the studio, published guides and Analytics are finger-sized, Ask AI rides on the keyboard, and a tap on a chart shows that day. See [Markdrop Guides and Analytics on phones and tablets](/changelog/guides-analytics-touch).
- Everywhere on a touch screen: buttons, menu items, tabs and fields are at least 44 points, text fields don't make an iPhone zoom in, and nothing reads under 12 points. Mouse and trackpad layouts are unchanged.

entries.title: Install Markdrop as an app
entries.summary: Markdrop installs on your phone, tablet or computer: its own icon and window, straight to your dashboard, a branded offline screen, and a Reload prompt when a new version is out. Markdrop Guides installs as its own app too.
entries.body:
- **Install app** in the account menu installs Markdrop in Chrome, Edge and Android browsers in one click, and shows the Add to Home Screen steps on iPhone and iPad (and File › Add to Dock in Safari on a Mac).
- The installed app opens on your **dashboard** (through sign-in when you're signed out), never the marketing pages, with shortcuts for **New page**, **Search**, **Markdrop Guides** and **Analytics** on its icon.
- Offline, it shows **You're offline** and reloads by itself when you're back. It keeps only its own code and icons on your device, never your documents or anything private.
- A new version shows **A new version of Markdrop is ready** with **Reload**, so you update when it suits you.
- On phones, bars, sheets and toasts stay clear of the notch and the home indicator.
- **Markdrop Guides** (guides.markdrop.in) installs as its own app that opens on your guides.
- See [Install Markdrop as an app](/get-started/install-app).

entries.title: The app on phones and tablets
entries.summary: My files, workspaces, folders, settings, sharing and search fit every phone and tablet: nothing scrolls sideways, every button is finger-sized, a tap anywhere on a row opens it, and menus open as sheets on phones.
entries.body:
- **Nothing scrolls sideways** on any screen, from a small Android phone to an iPad Pro. On a narrow phone **Create** shows just its plus, so the top bar fits.
- **Finger-sized controls**: buttons, menu items, tabs and fields are at least 44 points on a touch screen, and text is never smaller than 12 points. Text boxes use 16-point text, so iPhones don't zoom in when you type.
- **Tap anywhere on a row or card** in My files, Shared with me, Recent, a workspace or a folder's table to open it. Its own buttons still work.
- **Menus open as sheets** from the bottom of a phone's screen, over a dimmed page.
- **Boards on touch screens**: tap a card to open the page, or press and hold to drag it to another column. A long press on a row or card no longer opens the phone's link preview.
- A folder's views bar fades at the edge when more views are off screen.
- See [On a phone or tablet](/get-started/tour#on-a-phone-or-tablet).

entries.title: Pages, documents and files fit phones and tablets
entries.summary: A page's cover keeps its proportions on a tablet in portrait and on a phone, the New page gallery fits every screen and opens without the keyboard, and everything in a page is sized for a finger.
entries.body:
- **Covers** keep their proportions as the screen narrows: a tablet in portrait or a phone shows the whole cover, smaller, never a cropped middle of it.
- **New page**: the template gallery never runs off the side of a phone (a template's preview with a table used to widen it), lists the templates in one column on a phone, and on a touch screen opens on the templates, not in the title, so the keyboard doesn't cover them.
- **Touch screens**: the cover's tools, **Add icon** and **Add cover**, and an embed's **Show as**, **Replace** and **Remove** no longer wait for a hover. Every button in the page's bar, head and body is big enough for a finger, text fields never make the page zoom in, and nothing reads under 12 px.
- **Tablets** get the editing toolbar above the keyboard that phones have (add a block, the block menu, format, undo), as a bar in the middle of the screen.
- **Files**: an image opens fitted to the screen (tap it for full size), two fingers zoom a PDF's pages, and the video player and spreadsheets are sized for a finger.
- See [Colours, columns and block tools](/pages/blocks-and-layout#on-a-phone-or-tablet) and [Supported file types](/files/supported-types).

entries.title: Markdrop Guides and Analytics on phones and tablets
entries.summary: The Guides studio, published guides and Analytics fit a finger: every control is at least 44 px on a touch screen, text fields no longer make iPhones zoom, and the guide's bar gives the screen back on phones.
entries.body:
- **Touch sizes.** On phones and tablets every button, tab, menu item and field in the Guides studio, on published guides and in Analytics is at least 44 × 44 px, text fields are 16 px (iOS no longer zooms in when you tap one) and nothing reads under 12 px. Mouse and trackpad layouts are unchanged.
- **The guide's bar on phones** (and phones held sideways) scrolls away with the page instead of covering a third of the screen; the Live pill shows just *Live*.
- **Editor.** The page list opens without raising the keyboard, its rows and drag handles are full size for a finger, and the bar under the page has a Find button instead of keyboard shortcuts.
- **Ask AI on a published guide** rides on top of the on-screen keyboard on phones, so the question you're typing stays in view.
- **Charts in Analytics and Insights** show a day's numbers when you tap it, and keep them until you tap elsewhere.
- **Tablets.** On an iPad or Android tablet the guide's bar takes two rows instead of squeezing its buttons over its tabs, guide cards keep two columns until there's room for three, the studio header drops what the menus already show, and a published guide's Ask AI panel opens below the header in landscape.
- **Typing in the editor.** The + Block bar sits on top of the on-screen keyboard instead of under it.

entries.title: Add a sub-page offers your workspace's templates everywhere
entries.summary: Adding a sub-page to a page in a workspace now offers that workspace's templates wherever you start it: the page's menu, Pages inside, the sidebar and the workspace's own domain. A page in a folder with a default template starts its sub-pages from it too.
entries.body:
- **The workspace's templates for every sub-page.** **Add a sub-page** reads the templates from the page you're adding it to, so the sidebar's **+** and **Add a sub-page**, **Pages inside** and the page's **⋯** menu all offer its workspace's templates (to members of that workspace), yours and the built-in ones. Before, some of them showed only the built-in ones.
- **On your workspace's own domain** the gallery shows the workspace's templates and the built-in ones, and the sub-page can be made from either. Personal templates and managing templates stay on markdrop.in.
- **A folder's default template** is chosen for a sub-page of a page in that folder, like for **New page** there. Pick **Blank** or another template if you like.
- **AI apps:** `list_page_templates` takes `parent` to list what a sub-page of that page can start from, with its folder's default as `folder_default`.
- **API:** `GET /api/v1/page-templates/all` takes `parent` (a page's slug) and reads the workspace and folder from it.

entries.title: Import a meeting from a Google Drive link; Organizer is who ran the call; 1:1s stay private
entries.summary: Paste links to a call's Google Docs to import it: Markdrop reads a Doc shared with anyone with the link, and your Google Meet script fetches a private one. A meeting's Organizer is now who ran it (the Doc's owner in Drive), not who imported it, and 1:1s and two-person calls are restricted to their attendees on import.
entries.body:
- **Drive link** in the import dialog: paste one or more Google Docs or Drive links. Shared with "anyone with the link": imported right away. Private, with your Google Meet script connected here: **Queued**, fetched with your own Google access within 15 minutes. Otherwise Markdrop says how to give access.
- **Organizer and Imported by** are separate. Organizer is the Google Doc's owner in Drive (Google saves a call's Docs in the organizer's Drive), or who pasted text names ("Organizer: …"); otherwise it stays empty, never the importer. **Details** shows both; the page's **Organizer** property can be changed. Meetings imported earlier are corrected where Google said who owns the Doc.
- **1:1s and two-person calls are restricted to their attendees** when they're imported, on every path (manual, automatic, links, AI apps). Meetings of three or more stay with the team. Switch either way in **Details**.
- **Answers about meetings are steadier.** An answer can no longer come back empty or cut off when a question spans many meetings (**Catch me up** in Ask Markdrop could). Asking across meetings also reads the lines that name what the best match names (ask which email provider was chosen, and the line where someone takes on the migration comes too), and each quoted line backs only what it says.
- **Google's closing line stays out of the transcript.** "Transcription ended after …" is no longer added to the last thing someone said.
- **Covers.** Every meeting page has a cover from the gallery: one per series, so all the "Daily Syncup" meetings look alike, and a general one for one-offs. Meetings imported earlier get theirs too. A cover you chose or removed stays as you left it.
- **One item per meeting.** A meeting's Transcript no longer shows as a second item in folder views, folder counts and search. A word only said in the call finds the meeting page. The transcript is still under the meeting in the sidebar and linked from the page.
- **One series per name.** "Daily Syncup" and "Daily Sync Up" are one series (case, spaces and punctuation don't count). **Organize meetings** files meetings you already have, transcripts included, puts both spellings together and says how many meetings and series there are.
- **Sort by meeting date.** The Meetings page lists meetings by the day they happened, newest first, and can sort by oldest, title or recently imported. Your choice is remembered on the device.
- MCP `import_meeting` takes `drive_url`. API: `POST /api/v1/meetings/import-link` and `GET /api/v1/meetings/import-link`.

entries.title: Import past meetings, organised by date and series
entries.summary: Bring in weeks of earlier calls at once: drop all your transcripts and Gemini notes, check the dates in a review, and they import in the background, oldest first, each on the day it happened and without notifying anyone about old action items. Recurring meetings get their own folder (Meetings › Daily Sync Up), one-offs go to Other meetings, and Ask across meetings can stick to one series or period.
entries.body:
- **Import past meetings** on the Meetings page: drop or choose up to 300 files (transcripts and Gemini notes mixed), pick several Google Docs at once, or paste several meetings with a `===` line between them.
- **A review before anything is created**: each meeting's date (from Google's file name, the Doc's creation day or the text), its name and series, whether the notes and the transcript were both found, and whether it's already in the workspace. A meeting without a date is flagged until it gets one.
- **Runs in the background**, oldest first, and survives closing the page: "12 of 40", Pause, Resume, Stop, and Retry for a meeting that failed. A backlog bigger than today's Meetings AI budget waits for tomorrow's and carries on by itself.
- **Quiet**: action items in past meetings still @mention people, but nobody is notified about them.
- **A folder per series**: a meeting whose name comes back on another day ("Daily Sync Up", "Sprint 23 review" and "Sprint 24 review") gets a **Series** and its own folder, **Meetings › Daily Sync Up**; the earlier one moves in with it. Everything else goes to **Meetings › Other meetings**. Each folder opens on its meetings, newest first and grouped by month. Change a meeting's series in its Details and it moves; admins can **Organize meetings** to file the ones already there. The Meetings page lists meetings by month with a chip per series.
- **Who sees it**: 1:1s and two-person calls start restricted to the people who were there; calls with three or more people are open to the team. The review shows it, and you can change it per meeting.
- **Ask one series or a period**: pick them above the question, or say it ("What came up in the Daily Standups last month?"). Answers say when and where ("On 28 Oct, in Daily Standup…") and prefer recent meetings for questions about the latest state.
- **MCP**: `import_meetings_bulk` and `organize_meetings` (78 tools), and `list_meetings` and `ask_meetings` take a series and dates.

entries.title: AI answers no longer come back empty or cut off
entries.summary: AI search, Ask AI on guides, page AI, Analytics AI, meeting notes, auto covers, AI help in the Guides editor and AI-drafted fixes now leave room for the model to think before it answers. An answer that still runs long is asked for again with more room, or shows what it has with a note that it was cut short. It is never blank.
entries.body:
- **Why it happened.** The model behind Markdrop's AI features thinks before it answers, and that thinking counts toward the same length limit as the answer. Some features had limits sized for the answer alone, so on a harder question the thinking could use it all: the answer came back empty or stopped mid-sentence.
- **More room, same answers.** AI search, Ask AI on a published guide, page AI (summary, ask, rewrite, action items, title and description, alt text), Analytics AI (the weekly story, ask, content gaps and the document coach), meeting notes, AI help in the Guides editor and AI-drafted fixes all have room to think and answer. Each answer's length is still set by its instructions, so answers are no longer, and a normal answer costs the same.
- **Asked again once, never blank.** If an answer still runs out of room, Markdrop asks once more with a higher limit when nothing has been shown yet or the result must be complete (a rewrite, an analysis, notes). Otherwise you get what was written so far and a note that it was cut short. When nothing at all came back, it says so in words.
- **Quick picks skip thinking.** Turning a search into search terms and choosing a page's cover are simple choices, so they run without thinking: faster, and they can't come back empty.
- **Usage and limits as before.** Every attempt counts toward the same usage, cost and spending caps, including a retry. The same answers reach AI apps through MCP (`ask_documents`, `summarize_page`, `suggest_page_meta`, `ask_analytics` and the rest).

entries.title: A folder's Board shows its pages before it has a Select
entries.summary: Until a folder has a Select property, its Board view shows every page in one All pages column, with a button to add one, instead of an empty box.
entries.body:
- **Board** groups a folder's pages into columns by a Select property, like Status. Before the folder has one, the board now shows all its pages as cards in a single **All pages** column, so it never looks empty.
- A short note above the cards explains where columns come from, with **Add a Select property** for people who can change the folder's properties.
- See [Properties and views](/pages/properties-and-views).

entries.title: CLI 0.6.0: pages, exports, trash, access requests and search from the terminal
entries.summary: markdrop page creates, reads, edits and restores pages, with images from your disk; markdrop export saves them as files; and link set, trash, access and search bring the rest of your account to the terminal. The local MCP server gets two page tools.
entries.body:
- **`markdrop page`**: `new` (blank, from a template, or from a Markdown file or standard input, in a workspace and folder or inside another page, with its own slug), `get` (the Markdown with its front matter, or `--info`), `update` (with `--base-rev` so you never overwrite someone's newer save), `append`, `props` (icon, cover, layout, lock, export, and a folder's typed properties), `templates`, `image add` (an image file as inline Markdown, the cover or the icon), and `versions` / `version` / `restore` for the page's history.
- **`markdrop link set`** changes a page's, document's or file's link; the old link keeps redirecting. `--check` tells you whether a slug is free.
- **`markdrop export`** saves a page as Markdown, one HTML file or a zip with its images, with `--subpages` for its sub-pages. It never overwrites a file without `--force`.
- **`markdrop trash`** lists, restores and deletes: `rm` moves an item to the trash, `rm --permanent` deletes it forever after asking.
- **`markdrop access`** asks for edit access, lists the requests on your documents, and approves or declines them, with the same emails as the app.
- **`markdrop search`** finds the pages, documents, files, folders and workspaces you can open.
- Every new command takes `--json` and prints one JSON object.
- **Local MCP server**: `upload_page_image` puts an image file from your computer into a page, and `export_page` saves a page as a file. The local server now has 13 tools.

entries.title: AI apps can ask for edit access, and answer access requests
entries.summary: Three new MCP tools bring Request edit access and Access requests to your AI app: ask a page's owner to let you edit it, see the requests waiting for you, and approve or decline them, with the same rules and emails as the app.
entries.body:
- **`request_edit_access`** asks for edit access to a page, document or file you can open but not edit, with an optional note, just like **Request edit access** in the page's **⋯** menu. It goes to the owner, or to the workspace's admins when the page has no owner who can be reached.
- **`list_access_requests`** lists the requests waiting for you to answer (`incoming`, the default) or the ones you made (`outgoing`), pending, approved, declined or all.
- **`decide_access_request`** approves or declines one. Only the person who can answer in the app can answer here: the document's owner, or a workspace admin for an edit request sent to the admins. The requester gets the same email either way, and assistants are told to check with you before approving.
- The hosted MCP server now has 66 tools.

entries.title: Folder and workspace links unfurl with a card, and every Markdrop link has one
entries.summary: Paste a link to a workspace or a folder into Slack, WhatsApp or iMessage and it now unfurls with a card: its name, the workspace and how many items it holds. Every other markdrop.in link gets a Markdrop card too, and a private folder's card names nothing.
entries.body:
- **Folders and workspaces.** Links to a workspace or a folder (`markdrop.in/w/…`) and folder share links (`markdrop.in/f/…`) unfurl with a card: the folder's name, "A folder in Acme" and how many items are in it, or the workspace's name and its item count, in the workspace's brand.
- **Names only when a stranger could see them.** A card names a folder or workspace only when someone who isn't signed in could already see that name: a folder shared with anyone with the link, or a folder or workspace listed on the workspace's own domain. Every other one gets a card that says only "A folder in a Markdrop workspace" (or "A Markdrop workspace") and "Sign in to open it": no folder, workspace or domain name.
- **A cover on every link.** Any markdrop.in address without a card of its own, like the home page, **New document** or the README builder, now shows a Markdrop card instead of a bare link. Send-files links (`markdrop.in/share/…`) get a file-transfer card.

entries.title: Pages: one top bar, and a sidebar you can hide
entries.summary: A page now has a single bar at the top with everything in it: the app's header above it is gone. Hide the sidebar with ⌘ \ and peek at it from the left edge, and long menus scroll instead of running off the screen.
entries.body:
- **One bar.** On the left: the sidebar button, the logo (your workspace's logo on its own domain) and the breadcrumbs. On the right: who's viewing, **Saving…** or **Saved**, **Share**, **⋯**, **Create** and your avatar, or **Sign in**. It stays in place as you scroll, and on a phone the breadcrumbs fold to "… / Title". The theme switch moved to your avatar menu (to **⋯** when you're signed out).
- **Hide the sidebar** with the sidebar button or **⌘ \\** (**Ctrl \\** on Windows and Linux). Your browser remembers it, with no flash when the next page opens. While it's hidden, point at the left edge of the window to peek at it.
- **On smaller screens** the sidebar is a drawer that slides over the page from the same button.
- **Long menus scroll.** A menu is never taller than the room it has: a page's long **⋯** menu scrolls inside instead of running off the bottom of the screen.

entries.title: Who's viewing: see who's editing a page, and names only for people with access
entries.summary: The person editing a page now comes first in who's viewing, with a pencil on their avatar and "Riya is editing" in the bar. Viewers' names are now shown only to people who have access to the document: anyone else sees every viewer as an anonymous animal.
entries.body:
- **Who's editing.** On a page, the person holding it for editing gets an accent ring and a pencil and comes first in the row, and the bar says **Riya is editing** where there's room. On a phone the bar shows just their avatar with the pencil. When they stop, the pencil goes for everyone at once.
- **Names only for people with access.** You see viewers by name only if the document is yours, you're a member of its workspace who can open it, or it was shared with you. Anyone else, signed in or not, sees every viewer as an animal, your team included, and the editor as, say, **Anonymous Fox is editing**. Who's reading a team's page stays with the team.
- Someone who turned on **Show me as anonymous** is an animal for everyone, also while editing.
- Anonymous viewers have line-drawn animal avatars instead of emoji.
- AI apps: `get_viewers` follows the same rules and marks who's editing.

entries.title: A faster, cleaner sidebar
entries.summary: The sidebar now loads each workspace in one request and keeps it, shows pages with their emoji and documents and files with their kind, keeps what you have open in view, and shows + and ⋯ only when you point at a row.
entries.body:
- **One request per workspace.** A workspace's folders, pages, documents and files load in one go and stay loaded as you move around, so the sidebar no longer reloads or jumps when you open something. A folder shows up to 50 items, then "12 more".
- **Easier to scan.** Pages show their emoji, documents and files their kind's icon, in compact rows with guide lines. A name that doesn't fit shows in full when you point at it.
- **Where you are.** The page or folder you have open is highlighted and scrolled into view.
- **Quieter rows.** **+** (add a page inside) and **⋯** appear only when you point at a row. In the phone drawer they're large enough to tap.
- **Renames show at once.** Rename a page and the sidebar and page tree change straight away, in your other tabs too, without reloading.
- The page tree beside a page has the same icons, highlights the page you're on, and has **+** to add a page inside.
- API: `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/nav` returns the outline the sidebar shows.

entries.title: Mermaid diagrams show in the page editor and the Guides editor
entries.summary: A Mermaid block in a page or a guide now shows its diagram while you edit, just as readers see it. Click it to edit the code, with a live preview below; Esc shows the diagram again.
entries.body:
- **The diagram, not the code.** In the page editor and the Markdrop Guides editor, a `mermaid` code block draws its diagram, the same one readers get.
- **Click to edit.** Click the diagram, or press **Enter** on it, to edit its code. A preview under the code follows as you type. Press **Esc**, choose **Done** or click elsewhere to see the diagram again.
- **Errors stay readable.** If the code has a mistake, the block shows the error and the code.
- People who can only read the page, including on a locked page, always see the diagram.
- In a page, add one with **/** › **Mermaid diagram**; in a guide, set a code block's language to `mermaid`.

entries.title: Edit a document right in its Preview
entries.summary: When you edit a published Markdown document, the Preview tab is now editable: click into a heading, paragraph, list, table, code or math block and type. The Markdown stays the source, and blocks you don't touch keep their exact text.
entries.body:
- **Type where it renders.** Headings, paragraphs, lists, checklists, quotes, tables, code and math are editable in **Preview**. **Write** and **Split** work as before, and your changes carry across all three.
- **/** in Preview offers the blocks a document renders: text, headings, lists, checklist, quote, code, table, math and divider.
- **Nothing changes on its own.** Opening Preview and saving leaves the Markdown exactly as it was.
- Raw HTML and footnotes stay read-only in Preview: change them in **Write** (**Edit as Markdown** switches to it).
- **⌘ S**, **Save**, **Esc** and **Cancel** act on what you just typed. Past the 500,000-character limit, the status line says how far over you are and **Save** says so plainly.

entries.title: Fixes and polish: locked pages for admins, iPhone toolbar, templates and more
entries.summary: Workspace admins can edit, lock and unlock locked pages, the page editor's phone toolbar works on iPhones, a page you leave is free for others at once, and a round of smaller fixes.
entries.body:
- **Admins and locked pages.** A workspace admin can now edit a locked page in the editor, and lock or unlock it, as **Lock page** always said ("Only you and workspace admins can edit").
- **The phone toolbar on iPhones.** The page editor's toolbar above the keyboard works on iPhones and iPads (its buttons did nothing). Its **+** adds a block with the block menu open, and **/** opens the block menu in the middle of a line.
- **Leaving a page frees it.** Closing or leaving a page you were editing lets others edit it straight away, instead of two minutes later.
- **No more "Opening document" forever** on a page that needs sign-in.
- **Templates.** Renaming a template in **Manage templates** no longer also makes a blank page; double-clicking a template makes the page from that template; **Add a sub-page** offers your workspace's templates too; the note on a template page fits on phones.
- **Change link…** keeps the slug you're typing in view, with the full address shown below it.
- **Version history.** A restore that waits on someone's editing always says who; the selected version has a quieter outline, and a phone's version screen doesn't repeat the time.
- **Exports.** An exported HTML file uses the app's reading width, with tables in a rounded box, and a PDF keeps a coloured block's colour. Downloads stay in the tab you're in, even with a pop-up blocker extension installed.
- **A document that used to be a page** no longer shows its page settings as text at the top, and its owner and editors get the **Switch back to the page editor** banner.
- **Quick search (⌘ K)** shows each item's kind and link before where it is, and a workspace's grid tiles and cards show each item's kind, so a page and a file with the same title are easy to tell apart.
- **AI.** Clear messages when Markdrop's daily or monthly AI capacity is used up. On phones the AI sheet takes the focus and closes with **Esc**, and the AI button is its ✦. The workspace's **AI features** switch links to [AI in pages](/pages/ai) and says what's sent.
- **Beta badges.** Pages carry a **Beta** label wherever they're introduced.
- On a workspace's own domain, the **… on markdrop.in** links in a page's **⋯** menu no longer show a doubled arrow.

entries.title: Page exports look like the page, and a page stays a page
entries.summary: Exported HTML and PDFs no longer draw a page's title over its cover, exports always download or print where you are, and a page can no longer get stuck as a Markdown document.
entries.body:
- **Exports look like the page.** In the HTML file and the PDF, the cover runs across the top, the icon sits on the cover's bottom edge and the title is below them, never on the cover.
- **Exports stay where you are.** The file downloads in the tab you're in (or the print dialog opens there for a PDF), and if Markdrop refuses an export, the dialog says why. An AI app's export link that has expired opens a short page saying so, instead of an error.
- **A page stays a page.** **Open in the classic editor** is gone from a page's menus. **Edit as Markdown** shows the page's source only for now, with **Edit with blocks** on screen to go back; a reload always opens blocks again.
- **Switch back to the page editor.** A page that was switched to the classic editor shows its owner and editors a banner and a **More actions** item to make it a page again, on markdrop.in and on your workspace's own domain.

entries.title: Edit pages on your workspace's own domain, and Request edit access
entries.summary: Anyone who may edit a page can now edit it right on the workspace's own domain, like docs.acme.com, instead of going back to markdrop.in. Readers who can't edit a page can ask for edit access from its ⋯ menu.
entries.body:
- **Edit on your domain.** Signed in on the workspace's domain, a member, someone the page is shared with as **Can edit**, the owner or anyone with the edit link opens the page straight into the editor: text and title, images, sub-pages, page properties, AI writing tools and **Version history**, with **Saving…/Saved** and who's on the page.
- **Share with people on the domain.** Anyone who may share the page can see who has access, add people as **Can view** or **Can edit** (with **Notify people**), remove them and copy the link, right on the domain.
- Who can open it in general, its password and expiry, its link, deleting it, and workspace settings stay on markdrop.in, so a domain can never make a private page public: the owner's **⋯** menu opens the same page there (**General access on markdrop.in ↗**, **Change link on markdrop.in ↗**, **Delete on markdrop.in ↗**).
- The sign-in on your domain still works only there and only for that workspace's pages, and every page still runs its normal access check.
- **Request edit access.** Someone who can read a page but not edit it asks from the page's **⋯** menu, with an optional note, on markdrop.in or on the domain. The page's owner gets an email with **Approve** and **Decline** (the workspace's admins, when the page has no owner who can be reached) and an entry under **Access requests**. Approving lets them edit that page only; they get an email either way.

entries.title: AI in pages: rewrite, draft, summarize, translate, and ask a page questions
entries.summary: Pages have AI built in. Editors rewrite a selection, draft with /ai, turn notes into a page, find action items, summarize, translate a whole page and get alt text. Signed-in readers can ask a page questions.
entries.body:
- **Ask AI** on a selection (or **⌘ J**): improve, shorten, fix spelling and grammar, change tone, translate, turn into a checklist or a table, explain. Every result is a suggestion you accept or discard.
- **/ai** on an empty line drafts in the page's own blocks, with the page in mind. **New page › Start from notes** turns pasted notes into a structured page.
- In the page's **⋯** menu: **Summarize page** (a Summary note at the top), **Find action items** (to-dos with person and date chips), **Suggest title & icon** and **Translate…**, which makes a translated copy next to the page and leaves the original as it is.
- Images you upload get suggested alt text.
- **✦ Ask** for signed-in readers: questions about the page, answered from it and from the embedded items you can open, with links to the sections they use. It works on a workspace's own domain too.
- No AI for visitors who aren't signed in or for encrypted documents. Admins can turn **AI features** off for a workspace.
- Only the text a request needs goes to Anthropic, and Markdrop keeps usage counts, never the text. Fair use during the beta: 30 requests a minute and 300 a day per person.
- The same writing tools in the Markdrop Guides editor, and three new MCP tools: `translate_page`, `summarize_page` and `suggest_page_meta`. See [AI in pages](/pages/ai).

entries.title: Pages: version history, with changes highlighted and one-click restore
entries.summary: Every page keeps its earlier versions. Open Version history from the page's ⋯ menu to see each one as the page looked then, what changed against the page now, and restore any of them. A restore is itself a version, so it can be undone.
entries.body:
- **Saved for you:** one version per 10 minutes of editing and one when you leave the page, plus a version before and after every change an AI app makes, labelled with the app's name.
- **Version history** opens over the page: versions grouped by day, who saved each one, and the one that matches the page now. **↑** and **↓** step through them; on a phone, tap one to open it.
- **Show changes** highlights what's only in that version (green) and what's only in the page now (red, struck through).
- **Restore this version** asks first, then saves the restore as a new version, keeping the page as it was. It waits if someone else is editing the page.
- Every version is kept for 30 days, then the last one of each day for a year. Only people who can edit a page see its history. End-to-end encrypted documents have none.
- Images nothing in a page or its history shows any more are deleted after 30 days.
- New MCP tools: `list_page_versions`, `get_page_version` and `restore_page_version`.

entries.title: Export pages as Markdown, HTML or PDF
entries.summary: Download a page as portable Markdown, one self-contained HTML file or a PDF, with its images and the sub-pages you can open. Items a reader can't open are exported as "Locked item", never by name.
entries.body:
- **⋯ › Export…** on any page: pick **Markdown**, **HTML** or **PDF**.
- **Markdown** any app reads: callouts become labelled quotes, columns follow one another, people and dates become text, embedded files become links. With images, a `.zip` with an `images` folder.
- **HTML:** one file in the page's look, images inside, that opens anywhere, even offline.
- **PDF:** your browser's print dialog with the page laid out for paper: light, no menus, the cover on top, no blocks split across sheets.
- **Include sub-pages:** a folder for each one you can open, linked to each other; the PDF prints them after the page.
- **Readers can export** unless the page's editors switch that off in its ⋯ menu.
- An end-to-end encrypted document's browser saves its Markdown with **Download Markdown**.
- AI apps export with the new `export_page` MCP tool.

entries.title: Workspace templates: use any page as a template
entries.summary: Use a page as a template for your workspace or just for you, with its sub-pages and images. It shows up in New page and Add a sub-page, a folder can start every new page from one, and {{title}}, {{date}}, {{author}} and {{folder}} are filled in.
entries.body:
- **⋯ › Use as template** on any page: choose **Everyone in** your workspace or **Just me**, a name, a description and an emoji, and whether to include the sub-pages you can open. Images are copied with it.
- **New page** and **Add a sub-page** show your workspace's templates first, then yours, then the built-in ones, each with a preview.
- **A folder's default template:** admins choose what New page in a folder starts from, like a PRD template in `product-hub/02-prds`. Anyone can still pick Blank or another template.
- **Placeholders:** `{{title}}`, `{{date}}`, `{{author}}` and `{{folder}}` become the page's title, the day, the person making it and its folder.
- **Manage templates:** rename, edit (a template is a page, in the same editor), delete, and drag to reorder. Admins manage the workspace's templates; members can rename or delete the ones they saved. Editing a template never changes pages already made from it.
- Templates never show up in lists, search, the sidebar, folder pages or AI apps' document search. Viewers and people outside the workspace never see them.
- AI apps: `list_page_templates` (optionally for one `workspace`) lists them with ids, `create_page` takes a template's id or slug, `set_page_properties` with `template` turns a page into a template and back, and the new `save_page_as_template` and `set_folder_default_template` save one and set a folder's default.

entries.title: AI apps add image files and covers to pages, no base64
entries.summary: Your AI app can now add an image file from disk to a page, up to 20 MB, and make it the page's cover or icon. The file goes straight to storage with one curl command, instead of being pasted into the chat as base64.
entries.body:
- **`create_page_image_upload`** returns a storage address and the exact `curl` command that sends the file there; **`complete_page_image_upload`** checks the size, the SHA-256 and that the file really is a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image, then returns `asset:<id>` and the Markdown `![alt](asset:<id>)` to put in the page.
- **Covers and icons:** pass that `asset:<id>` to `set_page_properties` as `cover` or `icon`. Like every page image, it shows only to people who can read the page.
- **`copy_page_asset`** copies an image from one page to another you can edit, as a new image of that page.
- Images up to 20 MB this way; an upload not finished within 6 hours is discarded. `upload_page_image` still takes small images as base64, up to 10 MB.

entries.title: Pages: choose a page's link, and change it without breaking the old one
entries.summary: Change a page's link from its ⋯ menu, with the whole new address shown as you type. The old link keeps working on markdrop.in and on your workspace's own domain, and AI apps can set a page's link when they create it.
entries.body:
- **Change link…** in a page's **⋯** menu (owners): type the new slug, see it checked as you type and the full address it will have, with your domain, folders and parent pages.
- **The old link redirects.** On markdrop.in and on your workspace's domain, sub-page addresses included. Change it again and every earlier link goes to the newest one. Embeds and mentions of the old link keep working, with nothing to rewrite.
- **MCP:** `create_page` takes `slug`, the new `set_slug` tool changes the link of a page, document or file, and `publish_document` takes `editor: "blocks"` to publish a page. A taken link is an error that names it, never a silent rename.
- **API:** `POST /api/v1/pages` takes `slug`, and `GET /api/v1/documents/{slug}/slug-check?new_slug=` says whether a link is free and what the full address would be.

entries.title: AI apps can duplicate pages, list a workspace's members and mention people by name
entries.summary: Three additions for teams that build pages with an AI app: duplicate_page copies a page with its images, list_workspace_members gives the ids to mention people, and a mention written with just a name finds the member it means.
entries.body:
- **duplicate_page** copies a page you can read, with its properties and its own copies of its images, into a folder or page you choose, or next to the original. The copy is yours, and a locked page gives an unlocked copy, so a locked template can be the start of a new page. Sub-pages come along when you ask.
- **list_workspace_members** lists the members of a workspace you're in: name, account id and role, and email addresses for admins.
- In a page, `:person[Ada Lovelace]` without an id now finds the one member of the page's workspace with that name when the page is saved. A name that matches nobody, or more than one member, stays plain text, and the AI app is told which.

entries.title: Trash: everything you delete can be restored for 30 days
entries.summary: Deleting a document, page, file or folder moves it to Trash for 30 days instead of deleting it at once. Undo right after, or restore it from Trash, and it comes back exactly where it was.
entries.body:
- **Moved to Trash · Undo** right after every delete.
- **Trash** in the sidebar lists what you deleted: what it is and its link, where it was, who deleted it, when, and the days left. **Restore** puts it back with the same link, folder, parent page, access and people; **Delete forever** removes it for good.
- Deleting a **folder** moves it and everything inside to Trash; restoring brings the whole folder back. Workspace admins see and restore everything deleted from their workspace.
- The delete dialog now names exactly what goes: "Delete the page “Product Docs Playbook” (/EegpMKD)?", with how many sub-pages go with it. Lists show each item's kind next to its link, so two items with the same title are easy to tell apart.
- A deleted item's link stays reserved, and shows **This page is in the trash** (with **Restore**) to people who could edit it; everyone else gets the usual 404. Its files aren't served to anyone while it's in Trash.
- AI apps: `delete_document` moves to Trash and returns `restore_until`; new `restore_document` and `list_trash`; `permanent: true` deletes forever (owners, and admins for their workspace's Trash).
- `delete_document` deletes exactly the item at the slug or link it's given, never another item with the same title, and its result lists every item it removed (sub-pages first) and any sub-pages it moved up a level instead.

entries.title: Mentions that notify: a bell, emails and Notify people
entries.summary: Mention someone on a page and they're told: a notification under the new bell at the top of Markdrop, and an email, both opening the page at the block that mentions them. Only people who can open the page are notified.
entries.body:
- **The bell:** an unread badge, the list newest first with who, what, the page and when, **All** / **Unread** and **Mark all read**. Choosing one opens the page at the block and highlights it. A bottom sheet on phones.
- **Who's told:** each person newly mentioned (or named on a sign-off block) who can open the page. Never you, never someone already mentioned before your change, never someone who can't open the page, and a page they lose access to later shows without its title.
- **Email:** at most one per page every 10 minutes, with the mentions batched. Turn it off in **Settings › Account** (**Email me when someone mentions me**) or from the email's own link; the bell keeps working.
- **Share › Notify people** (was **Email them**): the email with your message, plus a notification for people with an account.
- **MCP:** pages an AI app writes notify the same way, and three new tools: `list_notifications`, `mark_notifications_read` and `share_with_people`. See [Mentions and notifications](/pages/mentions-and-notifications).

entries.title: Pages: sign-off blocks, approved by one named person and locked once signed
entries.summary: Add a Sign-off block to a page, name who signs it and give it options such as Approved for production or Not approved. Only that person can choose; Markdrop records the decision with their name and the time, and nobody can change the block, or the section above it, until they clear it.
entries.body:
- **/ › Sign-off** in any page in a workspace: choose who signs, the label and up to six options, and whether signing locks the section above.
- **Only the person named can sign**, not the owner, not an admin, not an AI app acting for someone else. The decision is stored by Markdrop, never in the page's Markdown, so it can't be faked by editing.
- **Once signed**, the block (and with *lock above*, everything from the previous heading down to it) can't be changed or deleted, in the editor, in Markdown, from VS Code or through MCP. The signer can change or clear their decision; a workspace admin can remove a signed block, and that's recorded.
- Sign-offs show on the block, as pills under the page's title and in **Version history** ("Signed off by Riya: Approved for production").
- Two new MCP tools: `list_signoffs` and `sign_off`. See [Sign-off](/pages/sign-off).

entries.title: Page properties, and folders as tables and boards
entries.summary: Give a folder's pages typed properties such as Status, Owner and Target date. They show under each page's title, and the folder opens as a table or a board: drag a card to change its status.
entries.body:
- **Properties under the title:** Select and Multi-select with coloured options, Person (a workspace member, with their picture), Date with a calendar, Text, Link (an address or a page), Number and Checkbox. Anyone who can edit the page changes them in place; readers see the ones that are set.
- **A folder is the database:** add a property once and every page in the folder has it. Members and admins add, rename and remove properties. Removing one never deletes a page's value.
- **Table and board views** in the folder: a sticky header, resizable columns, filter, sort and group, and cells you edit in place. On the board, drag a card between columns to change its value. Members save up to 20 views per folder.
- **Only what you can open:** views list just the pages you can read, and a linked page's title shows only to people who can open it.
- **For AI apps:** `set_folder_properties` and `list_folder_pages` are new, `set_page_properties` and `create_page` take `properties`, and `get_page` returns them. See [Properties and views](/pages/properties-and-views).

entries.title: Automatic covers for pages, and 32 new covers
entries.summary: A new page gets a cover picked for what it's about, from 44 calm covers now. Remove it in one click and it never comes back; workspace admins can turn Auto covers off.
entries.body:
- New pages get one of Markdrop's covers by themselves: AI reads the title and the first lines and picks one, or the page's words are matched when AI is off. It fades in a moment after the page opens. An untitled, empty page gets its cover once you've named it and started writing.
- 32 new covers, for roadmaps, meetings, releases, research, design, runbooks, people, finance, marketing, legal, support, data, security, docs and more, in a new **Shapes** group. **Pick for me** in the cover picker chooses one for the page.
- An automatic cover says **Auto** when you hover it. **Remove** is one click, and a removed cover is never added back. A duplicate keeps its original's cover; templates and encrypted pages never get one.
- **Auto covers** on the workspace settings' **Advanced** tab, next to **AI features**, turns it off for a workspace.
- Pages made before this got a cover the same way, once.
- MCP: `create_page` picks a cover (`auto_cover`, default true) and says which in `cover`; `set_page_properties` with `cover: "auto"` picks one again. See [Automatic covers](/pages/overview#automatic-covers).

entries.title: See who owns what in a workspace, choose List, Grid or Cards, and open folders instantly
entries.summary: A workspace's list now shows each item's owner with their photo or initial, and the people whose items are in each folder. Choose List, Grid or Cards; Markdrop remembers it. Folders open at once, even on slow connections.
entries.body:
- **Owners on every row.** Members see who owns each document, page and file, and **You** on their own. Folders show the people whose items are inside, and when something in them last changed.
- **List, Grid or Cards.** List is the default: name, kind, owner, updated, who can open it and **⋯**. Grid and Cards are tidier tiles with less text. Your choice is remembered on this device, everywhere in the workspace.
- **Folders open instantly.** Clicking a folder in the list, the sidebar or the breadcrumb switches right away, and items you pointed at are often already loaded. Pages no longer preload every link in the sidebar, so slow connections stay free for what you click.
- **Folder actions on the row.** Admins can rename, move, set what new items start as, or delete a folder from its row's **⋯** menu.
- **AI apps.** `list_workspace_items` says who owns each item, and `list_folders` says when each folder last changed and whose items are in it.

entries.title: See who works on each guide, and reach People in one click
entries.summary: Every guide on the Markdrop Guides home and in its bar now shows the faces of the people who work on it. Click them to open the guide's People. Members has its own button on the home.
entries.body:
- **Faces on every guide.** Cards and rows on the home show up to three people with a role on the guide (admins first) and **+n** for the rest; hover over a face for the name and role. Click the faces to open the guide's **Settings › People**.
- **In the guide too.** The guide's bar shows the same faces on every screen, one click from People.
- **People in every ⋯ menu.** Each workspace guide's **⋯** menu, in the cards and the list view, has **People**, and **Workspace members** for Guides admins.
- **Members on the home.** Guides admins find **Members** beside **New guide** at the top of the home.
